summary.intent: Orchestrate the GSD plan-phase and execute-phase workflows for CipherBox Phase 70.1 (rotation read-plane durability and deep crash-resume soundness), including two user-driven scope expansions (Rust engine.rs twin, desktop FUSE RotationDeps live-wiring), then execute all 13 resulting plans across 7 waves using worktree-isolated parallel subagents, culminating in a real desktop-e2e CI acceptance run.
summary.outcome: All 13 plans landed and merged with green unit/e2e gates (sdk-core 363, sdk 362, cargo cipherbox-sdk 146, cargo cipherbox-fuse 106); two genuine product bugs were found and fixed (dirty-frontier decrypt-before-check ordering in both engines, and missing desktop sent_shares refresh causing fail-closed EIO on all deletes). The final D-16 real-mount desktop-e2e CI run failed on macOS/Linux (Step 8 setup timeout) while Windows didn't even execute Step 8 (missing from run-all.ps1); a debugger investigating locally could not reproduce the timeout but found and is fixing an unrelated but real JsonSidecarFloorStore multi-writer race condition (ENOENT on rename) introduced by Plan 03's combined-sidecar design — fix still in progress at session end.

repo: GSD decision-coverage parser (.claude/gsd-core/bin/lib/decisions.cjs) only accepts three D-NN bullet forms (`**D-NN:**`, `**D-NN — title**`, `**D-NN: Title.**`); a bullet like `**D-NN (title).**` (period before closing `**`) causes ALL bullets in the file to be reported as 0/N covered, not just the malformed one
gsd_run loop render-hooks plan:pre --raw emits invalid JSON (literal newlines in fragments) — read the hooks file directly with Read instead of parsing --raw output
plan-phase never auto-commits PATTERNS.md — orchestrator must commit it explicitly after the pattern-mapper agent returns

state.planned-phase and roadmap annotate tools can silently no-op (return updated:[] / updated:false) when STATE.md/ROADMAP.md don't match their expected anchor fields — always verify with git status/git diff after calling them, don't trust the echoed success

CipherBox rotation gate keys off 'sent shares' (direct user-to-user grants via /shares/sent), not share-invites (claimable links); an unclaimed invite has granted no key access yet so isn't relevant to the scope-exit rotation decision

CipherBox delete is a soft-delete (moves to private recycle bin, re-seals keys under bin plane) — structurally equivalent to a cross-folder move, which is why it triggers scope-exit rotation just like a real move; same-folder rename does not rotate since parent==newparent

Rotation is forward-looking only — it re-keys the remaining tree but does not unpublish/re-encrypt already-published content CIDs (kept pinned for bin recovery), so a recipient who cached a key before deletion could still fetch that one old ciphertext out-of-band

crates/fuse crate has TWO independent gate-ordering/pattern implementations: crates/fuse/src/write_ops/implementation/*.rs (macOS/Linux, buildable) and crates/fuse/src/platform/windows/write_ops.rs (WinFsp, cannot even `cargo check` on macOS since winfsp-sys needs Windows COM APIs) — fixes must be mirrored manually to both, easy to miss the Windows side

desktop-e2e CI (.github/workflows/desktop-e2e.yml) has two separate harness scripts per platform: run-all.sh (macOS/Linux) and run-all.ps1 (Windows) — a new test step added to one is silently absent on the other unless mirrored explicitly

CipherBoxFS holds three independently-constructed JsonSidecarFloorStore instances (generation, seq, checkpoint) that all point at the same rotation-high-water.json file but each JsonSidecarFloorStore::new() builds its own separate Arc<Mutex<()>>, and write_map_atomic_blocking always writes to the same deterministic .tmp path before rename — concurrent writers race and the loser's rename() gets ENOENT

WriteQueue::load_all_for_vault and gc_failed_entries scan every *.json in cb-journal/ and try to deserialize as JournalEntry; the rotation-high-water*.json floor sidecar co-located there fails that parse (missing field 'id') and is warn+skipped every load/GC — benign (GC only deletes by entry.id from successfully-parsed Failed entries, orphan cleanup only touches .bin files) but noisy, pre-existing since Phase 69
GSD gsd commit helper can report commit_failed on a lint-staged timeout/false-negative even though the commit actually landed — memory-documented behavior: verify with git log, never blind-retry

code.finding: Every JsonSidecarFloorStore::new() call builds its own fresh Arc<Mutex<()>>, so multiple store instances pointed at the same underlying JSON path never actually share a lock — root cause of the ENOENT rename race across generation/seq/checkpoint stores.

write_map_atomic_blocking always writes to the same deterministic path.with_extension('tmp') then renames — with independent locks per store instance, two concurrent writers to the same underlying file collide on this shared tmp path.

collectDirtyFrontier/resolveChildKeyAndEnvelope unconditionally attempted AEAD-decrypt (unsealChildReadKey) of a child's sealed ref with the parent's current key BEFORE checking childPub.generation > childRef.generation (plaintext dirtiness check); for a genuinely dirty edge whose parent also rotated in the same walk, decrypt throws before the check ever runs. Fixed by reordering: fetch plaintext envelope, compare generations, only decrypt on confirmed-clean edges; dirty edges pushed to frontier with nodeReadKey: undefined and recovered via the ECIES checkpoint plane instead.

rotate_read_on_scope_exit originally stubbed as Err(RotationError::RotateFailed(...)) — fails closed (EIO) because the only impl RotationDeps in the workspace was the test FakeDeps; this was the documented LIVE-WIRING RESIDUAL deferred from the 69-13 summary, later wired to production FuseRotationDeps in Plan 09.

sent_shares was seeded to SentSharesCache::empty() at mount construction with no refresh call site anywhere in the codebase — combined with Plan 11's D-15a fail-closed fix, this made every desktop mount delete/rename return EIO regardless of private/shared status; fixed by wiring a bounded 5s initial refresh plus a 30s periodic background refresh via Arc<RwLock<>>.

workflow: When dispatching multiple worktree-isolated subagents, fire Agent tool calls one message at a time rather than batched in parallel — simultaneous `git worktree add` calls race on .git/config.lock; agents run concurrently in the background regardless of dispatch order once each worktree exists
Run a single-plan synchronous canary through the full worktree→commit→SUMMARY→merge cycle before fanning out a wave, especially when the harness has known worktree-merge failure modes

Scope cargo fmt to the specific package (-p <crate>) inside worktree executors, not workspace-wide `cargo fmt --all` — an unscoped fmt reformats unrelated out-of-scope files and leaves them uncommitted, blocking cleanup-wave merges with worktree_dirty

After merging a wave that touches a package whose dist other packages consume, rebuild all affected dists before running the next package's test suite — stale dist causes phantom cross-plan test failures that look like real regressions

Delegate diagnosis of a failing gate to a dedicated debugger subagent using strict scientific-method framing (must distinguish fixture bug from product bug, must not hack the test green) rather than debugging inline — keeps orchestrator context lean and produces an evidence-backed verdict
When a subagent's returned worktree_metadata expected_base doesn't match the wave's actual fork base, don't trust the label blindly — verify against the branch-check guard/manifest before merging

Avoid editing shared source files (e.g. queue.rs) in the orchestrator while a debugger subagent is running a live build/mount against the same checkout — compiling in an uncommitted change mid-debug can corrupt the debugger's diagnosis

Command-line numeric output can come back wrapped in ANSI color codes from Node.js colorized logging, causing naive string equality checks to falsely fail — strip escape codes or use a numeric comparison instead

friction: render-hooks --raw output was invalid JSON, forcing a workaround of reading the hooks file directly
decision-coverage gate failed opaquely (0/15 covered) due to a single malformed bullet elsewhere in the file, requiring manual regex archaeology to find the offending D-09/D-10 bullets
state.planned-phase and ROADMAP annotate tools silently no-op'd, requiring manual STATE.md edits and extra verification steps
Wave 1 cleanup-wave merge blocked on worktree_dirty caused by an unscoped cargo fmt --all leaving ~13 unrelated files reformatted and uncommitted in plan 03's worktree
Post-merge sdk vitest gate showed 3 false-positive failures caused by a stale sdk-core dist after a Wave 2 merge, requiring dist rebuild to confirm they weren't real regressions

sdk-e2e suite failed at setup with a 401 'Invalid test login secret' because vitest.config has no dotenv loader and the .env must be manually sourced into the shell before running — not obvious from the harness itself

Depth-3 sdk-e2e fixture (plan 10) exposed a real product bug (decrypt-before-dirtiness-check ordering) that unit-test mocks had been masking by making unsealChildReadKey unconditionally succeed regardless of key mismatch

Plan 13's static verification passed but the desktop mount's missing refresh_sent_shares call site meant the phase's core deliverable (D-16) would EIO on every real-world delete — a gap invisible to any of the automated non-live-mount test tiers
Live-mount desktop-e2e CI run failed on macOS/Linux at Step 8 setup (secret.txt propagation timeout) and didn't run at all on Windows because plan 13 only added the leg to run-all.sh, not run-all.ps1

A gsd commit helper 2-minute timeout on a large ROADMAP.md update (slow lint-staged hook) looked like a failure but the commit had actually landed, requiring git log verification per prior learned experience

JsonSidecarFloorStore multi-writer race could not be reproduced identically across two local debug runs — run #1 showed a different, unconfirmed anomaly (grant-root sequence bumped +2 instead of +1) suggesting the underlying race has multiple failure signatures
open_items: Fix JsonSidecarFloorStore multi-writer race: give all instances pointed at the same underlying path a shared Arc<Mutex<()>> (or per-call-unique temp filenames) — fixer subagent dispatched, in progress at session end

Apply the journal-sidecar-skip fix (skip rotation-high-water* filenames in WriteQueue::load_all_for_vault and gc_failed_entries scan loops) — root-caused and tracked as task #10, deferred until after the race fixer completes to avoid concurrent queue.rs edits
Commit the widened .mts poll-budget change (pollFindChild/pollSequenceBump 18→40 attempts + timing logs) once the fixer's crates/sdk commits land

Investigate the unconfirmed secondary anomaly from debugger run #1: grant-root sequence bumped +2 instead of +1 with a revocation-bypass-shaped result, possibly a symptom of the same un-serialized double-bump race
Re-push branch and re-run desktop-e2e CI across all three platforms once the race fix + poll-budget widening + Windows Step 8 are all committed, to get a genuine D-16 verdict
